transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I just can’t stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot right around my jaw and my neck. It's just really bothering me. Even when folks tell me it looks normal, I just don't see it that way. I feel like it’s the very first thing the families I work with, or the nurses, or even people at church notice when they look at me.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking or touching the area around your jaw and neck?

Yes, I do. Especially before I leave for work or... or even just going out. I keep going back to the bathroom mirror to check it. I'll adjust my collar, try to fix my hair around my neck to hide it... and then I'll pull out my phone camera to take another look. I even catch myself asking my daughter if it looks strange. It's... well, it's actually made me late more than once because I just can't stop checking.
Has your concern about the appearance of your jaw and neck affected your relationships or work performance?

Yes, it really has. At work... well, I’ve actually passed up a few chances to help lead meetings or take on some of the supervisory pieces. I just worry that if I'm up there talking, everyone will just be staring right at my face and my neck. And I’ve even fallen behind on my paperwork lately, because I get stuck trying to make myself look presentable instead of just sitting down and getting my tasks done. 

And outside of work... yeah. I’ve stopped going to some of my book club meetings, and I skip my walking club activities now, too. Just the thought of getting ready to see people feels like too much to deal with, so it's easier to just not go.
Is it just your jaw and neck that you're concerned about, or do you also worry about how other parts of your body look?

No, it's really just my jaw and my neck. I mean... I don't really worry about the rest of my body. I know I'm getting older, and things change, but none of that really bothers me. It's just this one specific spot that I can't seem to stop focusing on.
Do you think that your jaw and neck actually look uneven and sagging, or is it just that you feel like they should look different?

I... I really do think it looks sagging and uneven. That's actually why I came in to see you. I can't stop seeing it, and it feels so obvious to me. Sometimes people tell me it looks normal, but I just don't see what they see. I feel like it's the very first thing families or nurses at work notice when they look at me. Or even people at church. It just feels so noticeable.
Do you think your jaw and neck are actually defective in some way, or is it more that you're afraid they might look bad to others?

Well, like I was just saying a minute ago, I really do think there's an actual defect there. It's not just me being afraid of what people think. 

I just can't stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot around my jaw. That's really why I came in. Even when folks try to tell me it looks normal, I know what I see in the mirror. And because I see it so clearly, I just feel like it has to be the very first thing the families I care for, or the nurses at work, or the people at my church notice when they look at me.
Do you think you would still be concerned about the appearance of your jaw and neck if you were alone and never saw or interacted with other people?

I don't know... I guess I've never really thought about it like that. I mean, I look in the mirror and I see it, so it bothers me regardless of who else is around. But, I suppose if I knew for a fact no one else would ever see me... maybe it wouldn't feel quite so heavy. I'm honestly not sure, though. I just know what I see when I look at myself.
Would your concern about your jaw and neck go away if you were convinced that it looked normal?

I... I don't know. If I could actually see what other people say they see, and really believe it looked normal... maybe? But I just can't imagine that. Whenever I look in the mirror, the sagging is right there. It's so real to me. I don't know how I could ever be convinced it's normal when I can see with my own eyes that it's not.
Do you think you would still feel the need to check or hide your jaw and neck if you were certain that others did not notice or care about its appearance?

I'm really not sure. I mean, if I knew for a fact that nobody else cared or noticed... I'd like to think I wouldn't feel the need to hide it so much. But honestly, I just don't know if I could stop checking it. Because even if they don't see it, I still do. It's still there when I look in the mirror, so I think I'd probably still check it just because it bothers me so much.
Do you think your concern about your jaw and neck would decrease if you were in a situation where you knew you would not be evaluated or judged by others?

I really couldn't say for sure. I mean, it might take the edge off a little bit if I knew nobody was judging me. But... I'm the one who has to look at it every day. Even if no one else is evaluating me, I'm still evaluating myself. So I think it would still bother me a lot.
Do you think your concern about your jaw and neck would be less bothersome if you could be certain that it was not noticeable to others, even if you still saw it as uneven yourself?

I honestly don't know. I mean... maybe it would take a little bit of the stress away, knowing for sure that people aren't staring at it. But I'd still know it's there. I'd still see the unevenness every time I looked in a mirror or caught my reflection. So I'm really not sure if it would actually bother me less at the end of the day.
Do you think your distress about your jaw and neck is more because of how you think they actually look or because of how you fear others might react to them?

I honestly couldn't tell you which one it is more. It's... it's kind of just all rolled together for me. I really hate how it looks, just the actual shape and unevenness of it when I see it. But then, because I think it looks so bad, I constantly worry about what other people are thinking when they look at me. 

So I don't really know how to separate them to say which one causes more of the distress. I guess I'm just not sure.
Would your distress about your jaw and neck decrease if you were certain that others did not view it as uneven or sagging, even if you still saw it that way yourself?

I really don't know. I mean, it's hard to even imagine that, because to me it's just so obvious. But... if they really didn't see it? I guess I can't say for sure if I'd feel better. Because like I was saying before, I'd still be seeing the sagging and the unevenness myself. So I just don't know if my own distress would actually go down.
Is your distress about your jaw and neck more related to the fact that you think it's actually uneven, or because you're worried about what others might think of it?

Um... I think I'm still where I was a minute ago with that one. It's just really hard to separate them. 

I just don't know which one actually causes more of the distress. They just kind of feed into each other, you know? Hating how it looks makes me worry about other people seeing it. So, yeah, I really couldn't pick one over the other. I just don't have a clear answer for that.
If you were completely alone and had no interactions with others, would your distress about the appearance of your jaw and neck still be as severe?

I'm really not sure. I work around people all day, so it's hard to even picture being totally alone like that. I mean... I'd still have to look at myself in the mirror, so I know I'd still hate the way my neck and jaw look. But would it be exactly as bad as it is now, without anyone else around? I really couldn't tell you. I just don't know.
Do you think your distress about your jaw and neck would be less severe if you had no social interactions at all?

I honestly don't know. Like I said, it's just hard to imagine not being around people since I'm always working with clients. I'd still see it myself, so I'd still be upset about it. But if it would be less severe? I just can't say for sure.
Would you say that being around other people makes your distress about your jaw and neck worse?

I'm really not sure. I mean, maybe? But since I'm pretty much always around people at my job, the stress is just kind of constant. I don't really know if being around them makes it spike or get worse, or if it's just because I'm always thinking about my jaw anyway. It's just hard to measure since the feeling is always there.
Would your distress about your jaw and neck decrease if you were certain that it was not noticeable to others, but you still saw it as uneven yourself?

I really couldn't say. I mean, if I still saw it as uneven in the mirror, it would still bother me a lot. That's just how I see it. But if I knew for a fact no one else could see it... I don't know if that would actually make me feel any better or not. It's just really hard to separate the two things in my head.
Is your distress about your jaw and neck more about the fact that you think it looks bad or because you believe others will judge you for it?

I don't really know. I think it's both, honestly. I hate how it looks when I see myself, but I also worry a lot about my clients noticing it when I'm working with them. I couldn't tell you which one is worse, though. It just all kind of blends together into one big source of stress for me.
Would you say that your distress about your jaw and neck is more about the actual appearance or more about what you think others might think of it?

Like I was just saying, I really don't know how to separate them. I hate the way it looks, and I hate thinking my clients are staring at it. I honestly couldn't tell you which part causes more stress... I can't really pick one over the other. It's just all tied together.
